newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's MQM joins Sindh provincial cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's MQM joins Sindh provincial cabinet.

text.p: A Pakistani ethnic movement blamed in the past for turning Karachi into a battle zone joined the Sindh provincial cabinet on Thursday.
Seven members of the Mohajir National Movement (MQM) were among 16 Sindh cabinet members to be sworn in. Sindh Chief Minister Liaquat Jatoi has yet to announce their portfolios.
"We want to narrow the gap between the urban and rural Sindh population," Farooq Sattar, the MQM's leader in the provincial assembly, told reporters after the oath-taking ceremony.
Jatoi made a similar pledge and Sindh Governor Kamaluddin Azfar said: "I am very happy that urban and rural Sindh have joined hands and restored peace in the province."

The MQM, backed mainly by Urdu-speakers in Karachi and other cities in the south, has struggled for years to gain greater rights for Mohajirs, the term for those who migrated from India to Pakistan after the sub-continent's partition in 1947.

The militant tactics adopted by the MQM, led by London-based Altaf Hussain, have often led to conflict with past governments, including those led by present Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif and his main rival Benazir Bhutto, whose power base is in Sindh.
More than 500 people were killed in ethnic, sectarian and political violence in the southern port city of Karachi last year, compared to more than 2,000 in 1995 and 800 in 1994.
The Bhutto government, in power from 1993 to 1996, blamed what it called MQM "terrorists" for many of the killings.
The MQM accused the authorities of killing scores of its militants in cold blood, an accusation repeated by President Farooq Leghari when he sacked Bhutto in November.
The party emerged from February 3 elections with 28 seats in the 109-member provincial assembly, running second only to Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP), which won 35.
At the national level, it ranks third after Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League (PML) and the PPP.

The MQM and PML reached an agreement to form a coalition government in Sindh, shutting out the biggest party, the PPP. The MQM has seven ministers in the provincial government and the PML six. Two posts go to independents and one to former prime minister Ghulam Mustafa Jatoi's National People's Party.
Political sources said the MQM had dropped an earlier demand for its nominee to made provincial governor, but continued to insist on being given a portfolio in the national cabinet.
